hook: Twenty-six steamer trunks hidden in a basement revealed a forgotten history.

sections.voiceover: Twenty-six steamer trunks hidden in a basement revealed a forgotten history.
sections.visual_cue: Close up shot of an old wooden steamer trunk in a dark basement.

sections.voiceover: In 2005, Antonio Somera found twenty-six steamer trunks while cleaning out the basement of the Daguhoy Lodge in Stockton, California. What was inside those trunks?
sections.visual_cue: Archival photograph of Antonio Somera and the Daguhoy Lodge exterior.

sections.voiceover: Inside twenty-six steamer trunks, the Legionarios del Trabajo preserved decades of farm worker histories, but they nearly vanished.
sections.visual_cue: Historical photographs of farm workers arranged on a table.
b_roll: Legionarios del Trabajo members archival portrait

sections.voiceover: Visitors at the National Museum of American History see three of the twenty-six steamer trunks.
sections.visual_cue: Museum exhibit display showcasing three steamer trunks behind glass.
b_roll: National Museum of American History interior

sections.voiceover: Twenty-six steamer trunks preserve the past at the Smithsonian Asian Pacific American Center.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the museum exhibition entrance sign.
b_roll: Smithsonian Asian Pacific American Center logo and display
